1	# Voice call research: roadmap
2	
3	For anyone (person or agent) picking up work on branch `t3/research-self-hosted-voice`. Read this first, then the part of `LOG.md` your package points to. `LOG.md` is the full history with every measurement; this file is only what is true now and what to do next.
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	A voice call for Moneo that is better than a general voice model for this job, built from small parts that can be swapped (speech-to-text, the "editor" that understands the request, text-to-speech, any chat model behind it), and able to run on a laptop.
8	
9	The idea that makes it different: **the call keeps one typed object and every spoken word edits it.** For a question the object is a question card (what, where, when) that Moneo's own code answers. For "add this" it is a draft of the record, shown as a card the owner taps. A correction ("no, last month", "not Rewe, Lidl") edits the object instead of starting over. Anything the object cannot hold goes to the chat model, exactly as the call works today.
10	
11	It has to work for **any owner, not just the first one**: other accents, other ways of asking, other shops, currencies and languages. Rules tuned on one voice do not count as done.
12	
13	## Where things stand
14	
15	| Piece | State | Evidence |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| Question card, editor rules, exact money in words | built, tested | `lib/ai/voice-query*.ts`, `voice-say.ts`; LOG 8 |
18	| Code answers call questions before the chat model | built, on by default behind Settings switch "Quick answers in calls" | `voice-fast-path.ts`, `app/api/chat/route.ts`; LOG 10, 12 |
19	| "Add" draft with corrections, becomes a tap-to-save card | built for one-off spending and income with a known shop or category | `voice-draft.ts`; LOG 14, 15 |
20	| First real recording (one speaker, 18 requests) | code handles 6 of 18 right with a good transcript, 5 with Whistle; 1 wrong card from number formatting | LOG 13, 14 |
21	| Generated test sets (500 cases) | 99%, but they were too clean: 0 of 18 on first contact with real speech | LOG 8, 13 |
22	| Speech-to-text on real voice | Whistle 19% of words off, Whisper base.en 11% at the same speed | LOG 13 |
23	| A spoken call through GPT-Live with the fast path | **not tested**: the OpenAI key on the dev laptop has no credits | LOG 12 |
24	| Ears (talking over the assistant), local speech engine, changing an answer mid-sentence | not built; only simulated measurements | LOG 2 |
25	
26	The honest summary: the typed-object idea works and is safe (it hands off instead of guessing), but hand-written rules and a tiny recogniser are not good enough for real speech. The next gains come from real test data, a learned extractor and a better recogniser.
27	
28	## Rules for working here
29	
30	1. **Safety of money.** Code on the fast path only reads. A write is only ever a card the owner taps (`agent_proposals`). Never create, change or accept a record from speech directly, and never act on words that are still arriving.
31	2. **Never guess.** A question is answered by code only when every word is explained; a draft is shown only with a clear amount and something the owner already has. Otherwise return null and let the chat model take the turn. A wrong spoken number is the worst failure there is.
32	3. **Test backend only.** Follow `AGENTS.md`: use `moneo-qa` (`.env.qa`), never the owner's data. Recordings and transcripts are personal data: keep them outside the repo and commit only scripts and totals.
33	4. **Real speech is the test.** Generated cases are a regression check. A change counts when it moves the real-recording scoreboard without adding a wrong answer.
34	5. **Write down what you measured, including failures,** in `LOG.md` as a new numbered section. Say what was not measured.
35	6. **Commit every small step** on this branch with a plain message. Do not push, open a pull request or merge unless asked.
36	7. **Keep parts swappable.** Nothing may assume one recogniser, one voice or one chat model.
37	
38	## How to run things
39	
40	All from the repo root. `npm ci` first.
41	
42	| What | Command |
43	|---|---|
44	| Unit tests for this work | `npx vitest run lib/ai/voice-query.test.ts lib/ai/voice-draft.test.ts lib/ai/voice-call-controller.test.ts` |
45	| Everything before finishing | `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` (`components/ai-message-remount.test.tsx` sometimes times out under load; rerun it alone) |
46	| Editor on the generated sets | `node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs research/voice-duplex/experiments/expE/eval_editor.ts dev\|test\|v2 [--show]` |
47	| A recording: split, transcribe | `experiments/expF/split.py <audio> <folder>`, then `transcribe.py <folder>` and `reference.py <folder>` (Python with `av`, `silero-vad`, `cactus-compute`, `faster-whisper`) |
48	| A recording through the editors | `.../expE/real_call.ts <folder>` (questions), `.../expE/real_adds.ts <folder>` (adds) |
49	| Test backend | `npm run setup -- --qa`, then `npm run qa:auth` |
50	| Made-up data for it | `node --env-file=.env.qa node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs research/voice-duplex/experiments/expE/voice_test_seed.mts` (`--remove` undoes it) |
51	| This branch on port 3101, no AI cost | `node research/voice-duplex/experiments/expE/qa_server_3101.mjs` |
52	| Call turns as text through the real route | `node research/voice-duplex/experiments/expE/call_turns_qa.mjs --owner "first turn" "second turn"` |
53	| Same server with a real OpenAI key (spoken test, costs money) | `voice_test_server.mjs`, then `voice_test_report.mts` |
54	
55	## Code map
56	
57	| File | Job |
58	|---|---|
59	| `lib/ai/voice-query.ts` | Question card type, spoken periods to exact dates, card to `investigate()` input |
60	| `lib/ai/voice-query-editor.ts` | `editCard(base, words)`: rules that edit the card; `leftover` = unexplained words |
61	| `lib/ai/voice-draft.ts` | `editDraft(base, words)`: draft of an add; `draftProposal()` = input of `transaction_propose` |
62	| `lib/ai/voice-say.ts` | Money in words, the answer in pieces with the number last, `rebind()` |
63	| `lib/ai/voice-fast-path.ts` | `voiceFastTurn()`: one call turn for code, or null |
64	| `lib/ai/voice-fast-answer.ts` | The same in memory, without a database (used for timing; the local engine will need it) |
65	| `app/api/chat/route.ts` | Tries `voiceFastTurn` on a call turn, makes the card for a draft, falls back to the model |
66	| `lib/ai/voice-call-controller.ts` | Browser side of today's call; keeps the card or draft between turns |
67	
68	## Work packages
69	
70	Each one can be taken by a different agent. "Needs" lists what must exist first. Every package ends with numbers in `LOG.md` and an updated row in the table above.
71	
72	### A. The real test set and one scoreboard (do this first; everything else is judged by it)
73	
74	- **Why:** there are 18 real requests from one speaker. That is too few, and one voice says nothing about other people.
75	- **Build:** a folder layout for recordings outside the repo (`<speaker>/<session>/` with clips, transcript, and a small label file per clip: kind = question / add / other, and the expected card or draft). One command that runs every speaker through recogniser + editors and prints: right, wrong, handed off, per speaker and per kind, plus word errors on the reading script.
76	- **Other speakers:** `reading-script.md` can be read by anyone. Also add public accented-English speech for the recogniser (for example Common Voice, L2-ARCTIC), and many written phrasings per intent from different writers and models for the editors. Report every score per speaker, never only the average.
77	- **Done when:** at least 5 speakers and 150 labelled real requests; the scoreboard runs with one command; today's numbers are recorded as the baseline.
78	- **Needs:** recordings from people. Nothing else.
79	
80	### B. Learned extractor (replace the hand rules for finding things)
81	
82	- **Why:** rules went from 0 to 4 of 18 only after seeing the recording. That repeats with every new speaker.
83	- **Build:** a small model that tags the words of an utterance (amount, shop or description, category, account, period, comparison, metric, "this replaces that") and its kind (question / add / other). Train it on generated speech written in the style of real recordings (long, greetings, restarts, corrections, many personas, currencies and shop lists), labelled by a large model, and on the real set's training half. The rules stay as the checker that turns tags into a card and decides whether code may answer.
84	- **Sizes to try:** a token classifier around 20 to 60 MB on CPU first; a fine-tuned tiny generative model only if tagging cannot express corrections.
85	- **Done when:** on real speakers it was not trained on, it beats the rules on handled-right without more wrong answers, and runs in under 20 ms per update on a laptop CPU.
86	- **Needs:** A.
87	
88	### C. More kinds of drafts
89	
90	- Recurring payments ("24 euros a month for ChatGPT" maps to `recurring_propose`), balances ("17 euros in my wallet" maps to `balance_propose`), loans (`iou_propose`), and adds without a known shop ("train ticket to Munich", needs B for the description).
91	- Fix known: amounts must come from the recogniser's raw words, and the owner's currency wins over a symbol nobody said (LOG 14, the wrong salary card).
92	- **Done when:** each kind has tests written from real sentences and a row on the scoreboard.
93	- **Needs:** nothing for recurring and balances; B for free descriptions.
94	
95	### D. More kinds of questions
96	
97	- Balances, net worth, recurring list, budget left: thin wrappers over what exists (`getBalances`, `readNetWorth`, `listRecurring`, `budgetProgress`), each with its own one-sentence answer and its own "cannot say this truthfully" exit. Several periods in one question ("this month and last month").
98	- **Done when:** each has tests and a scoreboard row; wrong answers stay at zero on the real set.
99	- **Needs:** nothing.
100	
101	### E. The recogniser
102	
103	- Bench small recognisers on the real set, not on synthetic speech: Whistle, Whisper tiny/base/small, Moonshine, Parakeet-class models. Measure word errors, key words kept (shops, "euros", "add", numbers) and time, per speaker, streaming where the model allows.
104	- Try, in this order: the owner's names as hints, a second pass that repairs unexplained words against the owner's names and the card's grammar ("years" after a number where a currency is expected), and adapting a tiny model to one voice from the reading script.
105	- **Done when:** one recommended default and one "tiny" option, with numbers per speaker, and a single interface so they can be swapped.
106	- **Needs:** A.
107	
108	### F. Ears: hearing the owner while the assistant talks
109	
110	- Real microphone and speaker on `moneo-qa`, at least 3 speakers, 40 corrections and 40 "mm-hm" over playback. Echo cancelling plus a detector that also gets what is being played.
111	- **Pass bar:** 90% of interruptions caught within 0.4 s, the words of the correction right 85% of the time, false stops at most 10%. Simulated results so far: about 1 s to stop and 6 of 24 missed (LOG 2).
112	- **Needs:** E for the words; nothing for the harness.
113	
114	### G. The local engine behind a setting
115	
116	- Speech in and out on the laptop, emitting the same events the call uses today so the rest does not change. GPT-Live stays selectable (it also speaks German).
117	- Constraints: route handlers cannot hold a WebSocket and the proxy buffers bodies, so use a side port or run models in the browser; everything listens on 127.0.0.1; the desktop app ships no Python; the repo is MIT, so ship a permissively licensed voice and make Woof an optional download.
118	- **Pass bar:** first sound under 0.5 s median; numbers spoken right 99% of the time.
119	- **Needs:** E, F.
120	
121	### H. The live card and changing an answer mid-sentence
122	
123	- Show the card or draft filling in on screen while the owner is still talking. Start speaking the lead-in of an answer early and change what comes next when a correction arrives (`rebind()`), with a check that the number about to be played is the number in the card.
124	- **Pass bar:** listeners prefer it to stop-and-restart (about 12 listeners); a wrong number reaches the speaker in under 1% of turns.
125	- **Needs:** G for speech; the on-screen part needs nothing.
126	
127	### I. Scoring and write-up
128	
129	- The same script against today's GPT-Live call, measured, not quoted. Public tests for changing your mind mid-sentence and talking over the assistant (Full-Duplex-Bench v3, EchoChain).
130	- The claim to defend: a full-duplex call whose state is a runnable typed object, updated on every word including overlapped speech, on a laptop CPU, with fewer wrong numbers and better handling of corrections than a general voice model. Earlier work to credit is listed in LOG 5 and 7.
131	- **Needs:** A to H as far as they got.
132	
133	## Order and what can run side by side
134	
135	```
136	A (test set) ──┬─> B (learned extractor) ──> C free descriptions
137	               └─> E (recogniser) ──> F (ears) ──> G (local engine) ──> H (mid-sentence)
138	C recurring + balances, D questions: can start now, in parallel
139	I: last
140	```
141	
142	## Open decisions for the owner
143	
144	- Add OpenAI credits (or another key) so a spoken call through GPT-Live can be tested.
145	- Who else can record: the reading script plus five minutes of free talk per person.
146	- Whether the fast path should go to `main` on its own before the rest (it is behind a Settings switch).

## 13. First real recording from the owner (2026-11-16)

One 251 s phone recording with 18 spoken requests, said the way the owner really talks. Audio and transcripts stay outside the repo (`<home>/moneo-voice-tests/call1`); only the scripts are here (`experiments/expF`, `experiments/expE/real_call.ts`). Split at pauses of 1 s with Silero VAD, transcribed with Whistle and, as a reference, Whisper large-v3-turbo (no human transcript exists, so "difference" below is against that reference, which favours Whisper-family models).

What the owner actually asks (18 requests):

| Kind | Count | Examples (paraphrased) |
|---|---|---|
| Add something | 8 (44%) | "I spent five euros at Rewe for groceries, add that", a subscription, a train ticket, cash in the wallet, a salary |
| Read a number | 5 (28%) | spending this month, last month, earnings from salary this year, groceries for the whole year |
| What-if, advice, other tools | 5 (28%) | change jobs, cancel one subscription for another, "is this above my median", check the broker |

Findings:

1. **Coverage on first contact was 0 of 18**, even with the reference transcript, against 99% on the generated test sets. Nothing was answered wrongly; every turn was handed to the chat model. The generated sets were too clean: real requests are long (mean 8 s, up to 18 s), start with a greeting or context, and use "can you check / find out / I wanted to ask".
2. **Every self-correction in the recording (4 of 4) was inside an "add" request**: the shop ("not Rewe, Lidl"), the amount twice ("not ten, twenty", then in a new turn "not even twenty, twenty-four"), and an estimate replaced by the real price. The question card cannot hold any of these. The thing people correct mid-sentence is the draft of a new record, not the query.
3. **A wrong answer the generated sets never produced**: after "earnings from salary this year", the whole question "can you check how my groceries are for the whole year" was treated as an edit of the previous card and became "income, Groceries". Fixed: a whole question without a money verb starts a new card. Also fixed: "this month and also last month" is two questions and goes to the chat model; "the whole year" is a period; "wanted, ask, check, find, exactly" are harmless words.

2. **A learned extractor** next. Hand rules went from 0 to 4 of 18 only after seeing the recording; that will repeat with every new speaker and phrasing. # Where the voice research branch is now

**Branch:** `t3/research-self-hosted-voice`. It has 11 commits, all local. Nothing has been pushed and no pull request is open. The short version: the core idea works and is safe, but it has only been checked against one real recording. Your two new recordings are the next input.

## The idea in one line
A call keeps one "card" on the screen and every sentence you say edits it. For a question, Moneo's own code reads the exact number from your data. For "add this", the card is a draft that you tap to save. When you correct yourself ("no, Lidl, not Rewe"), the card changes instead of starting over. Anything the card can't hold goes to the chat model, the same way calls work today.

## The sections (work packages A–I)

| # | Section | Status |
|---|---|---|
| — | **Question card**: turns "how much did I spend on groceries last month" into an exact query, and says money in words with the number last | ✅ Built and tested |
| — | **Quick answers**: code answers simple call questions before the chat model is asked (about 0.3 s). Settings switch "Quick answers in calls", on by default | ✅ Built |
| — | **Add drafts**: "I spent 5 € at Rewe" becomes a tap-to-save card; "not Rewe, Lidl" swaps the card | ✅ Built, but only for one-off spending or income at a shop or category you already have |
| **A** | **Real test set and one scoreboard**: recordings from several people, labelled, scored with one command | 🟡 1 of at least 5 speakers (18 requests out of a target of 150). **Your 2 new files feed this.** |
| **B** | **Learned extractor**: a small model that finds amount, shop, period and so on, instead of hand-written rules | ⬜ Not started (needs A) |
| **C** | **More draft kinds**: subscriptions, cash in the wallet, loans, adds with no shop ("train ticket") | ⬜ Not started. There is also a known bug: "1,343 euros" became a dollar amount |
| **D** | **More question kinds**: balances, net worth, budget left, recurring payments, two periods in one question | ⬜ Not started (can start now) |
| **E** | **Speech recogniser**: pick the best small model on real voices | 🟡 Measured on your voice only: Whistle gets 19% of words wrong, Whisper base.en 11% at the same speed |
| **F** | **Ears**: hearing you while the assistant is talking | ⬜ Only simulated: about 1 s to stop, 6 of 24 interruptions missed |

| **I** | **Scoring against GPT-Live and the write-up** | ⬜ Last |

## The real numbers so far
- **Your first recording (18 requests):** code handled 6 correctly. It gave 1 wrong card, the salary amount, caused by how the recogniser wrote the number. The other 11 went to the chat model, which is safe.

4. **What comes after scoring the files:** D (more question types), C (subscriptions and cash drafts), B (learned extractor) or E (recogniser)? My recommendation is C plus the salary-amount fix first, because your recording showed that adds are where most of your requests and all of your corrections are.

# Reading script for voice tests

Sentences and short conversations with known words, so a recording of them can be scored exactly. Anyone can read it: every extra voice (accent, speed, microphone) makes the test set better. It takes about 15 minutes in all.

How to record:

- One recording per part, on a phone or laptop, in a normal room. Name the files `<your name>-part1.m4a`, `-part2`, and so on.
- Do not say the numbers or the labels. Just leave the pauses described for each part.
- Speak the way you normally would, not slowly or carefully. If you stumble, carry on; do not repeat.
- Say the names as written (Rewe, Lidl, Netto, and so on), even if you shop somewhere else: the test knows these names.
- Send the files to the owner privately. Recordings are personal data and are never committed to the repository.

## Part 1: single requests (about 3 minutes)

Understood. The free-talk requests no longer decide what gets built next; they only stay in the tests as a check that code never answers them (logged in `LOG.md` and committed).

**No model of our own, and no training from scratch.** Every learned part starts from an existing open model, either fine-tuned or with a small layer trained on top.

## What I've already done with models (all in experiments, nothing in the app yet)

| Part | What was done | Weights changed? | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| **The streaming model you remember: Woof, the voice that speaks** | Wrapped it so it starts talking after about 0.1 s instead of 1–3 s. It produces the same sound, just in chunks. | No, it's a wrapper | `experiments/` (exp C), LOG 2 |
| **End-of-turn detector** ("has the owner finished talking?") | Took Whistle's internal speech representation (the "embedding") and trained a tiny layer on top: 1,500 numbers, 92.7% accurate. The existing Smart Turn model did 95%, so it's the current choice. | Only the tiny layer; Whistle untouched | exp A, LOG 2 |
| **Router** ("question, add, or small talk?") | Tried a text-embedding model plus a small classifier: 79%. A simple word-count classifier did 86% and was 200× faster, so the embedding approach lost. | Small classifier only | LOG 2 |
| **The voice-call code on this branch** | Hand-written rules, no learning. | — | `lib/ai/voice-*.ts` |

So the speaking model is streaming already. Nothing has been fine-tuned yet.

## What I'll do with the recordings

**1. Use them as the test set first.** About 60 of your requests plus your friends' are far too few to train on. Their main job is to be the honest exam that every change is scored against. Anything I train on never comes from the half I test with.

**2. Recogniser (speech to text): fine-tune Whisper base.en.** This is the part that changes a model's weights.
- First, two cheaper fixes with no training: give the recogniser your shop names as hints, and add a repair pass afterwards. For example, "years" after a number where an amount is expected becomes "euros".
- Then a light fine-tune (LoRA, a small add-on to the model's weights) of Whisper base.en. It's trained on read speech from you and your friends, plus public accented-English recordings (Common Voice, L2-ARCTIC) so it doesn't only learn your voice. It's small enough for this laptop.
- Pass bar: fewer wrong words on speakers it was not trained on.

**3. Extractor (finding amount, shop and period in a sentence): fine-tune a small text model.**
- An existing small model of about 20–60 MB, taught to tag the words of a sentence.
- It's trained on many generated sentences written to sound like your real ones: long, with "um", restarts and corrections. A large model labels them.
- The current rules stay as the safety check that decides whether code may answer.

**4. Interruptions: the embedding approach again.** Same as the end-of-turn detector: keep the recogniser as it is and train a tiny layer on its embedding. It learns "real interruption" versus "mm-hm" versus the assistant's own voice coming back through the speaker. Part 3 of the new script, where a second person reads Moneo's lines, is the data for this.

**Order:** 2 → 3 → 4. The recogniser is the biggest weakness right now: Whistle gets 24% of your words wrong and loses "euros", "Rewe" and "Lidl". Part 2 can start now on your reading recording and public data. Your friends' recordings make the fine-tune and the exam fair.

One thing is unfinished: the full test, lint and typecheck run was stopped partway. The voice tests (57) passed, but I'll rerun the whole suite before more work.
